subject: COBOL words
notes: kb/Work PB1405 (registrar 15b). Rule: `OK §8.3.2.2 1)` "When the COBOL call convention is implied or COBOL is specified in a CALL-CONVENTION compiler directive, that method-name is treated as a COBOL word that maps to the externalized name of the method to be invoked, applying the same implementor-defined mapping rules as for a method-name for which no AS phrase is specified." (context: "When an INVOKE statement or an inline method invocation references a method-name using a universal object reference:"). The COBOL convention is always in force here (`OK §7.3.9.3 1)` "The default for the CALL-CONVENTION directive is '>>CALL-CONVENTION COBOL'."; >>CALL-CONVENTION is recognized-and-ignored). EXPECTED: the universal INVOKE's method-name reaches the method whose EXTERNALIZED name it maps to — the same answer the typed path gives, since the class's COBOL entry convention makes the mapping identical. OBSERVED (out/probe/callconv, class MICLS with METHOD-ID. M1. and METHOD-ID. M2 AS "MixedExt"., --std 2023; mi_a also at 2002): universal U: INVOKE U "m1" -> M1 RAN (correct); INVOKE U "M2" (mi_a) -> M2 RAN — WRONG, "M2" is the DECLARED word, not the externalized name; INVOKE U "MixedExt" (mi.cob), U "MIXEDEXT" (mi_e), and identifier-2 holding "MixedExt" (mi_d) -> abnormal termination EC-OO-METHOD 'does not implement a method named MIXEDEXT' — WRONG. The typed twin agrees with the spec: INVOKE T "MixedExt" (mi_b) -> M2 RAN, INVOKE T "M2" (mi_c) -> COBOL0825. Cause: OoEmitter.EmitCobolInvoke labels each __CobolInvoke switch case with m.Name.ToUpperInvariant() — the declared method-name — while the static typed path (PB303, conformance:cases/8.3.2.2-User-defined-words/pb303_as_module_name_and_invoke) resolves by the AS literal.
